newsitem.title: CAMBODIA: Cambodian foreign minister appointed first premier.
newsitem.headline: Cambodian foreign minister appointed first premier.

text.p: Cambodian Foreign Minister Ung Huot was formally appointed first prime minister on Thursday, replacing the ousted Prince Norodom Ranariddh, the country's acting head of state said.

The appointment came after King Norodom Sihanouk said acting head of state Chea Sim could issue a decree appointing Ung Huot in place of Ranariddh, the king's son, who was overthrown in a bloody coup on July 6.

"His Excellency Ung Huot is the first prime minister of the royal government of the Kingdom of Cambodia instead of (His Majesty) Prince Norodom Ranariddh," Chea Sim said in a decree read over national radio and television.
Powerful Second Prime Minister Hun Sen, who overthrew Ranariddh, backed Ung Huot's nomination and it was approved by parliament on Wednesday.
The U.S. Embassy in Phnom Penh said the parliament's vote was undemocratic given the climate of intimidation in the country following Ranariddh's ouster.

Sihanouk, who is in Beijing for medical treatment, told Chea Sim on Thursday that he could approve Ung Huot's nomination. The king is required by the constitution to approve a new first prime minister.
